content:
emma: customer AcmeCorp reports repeated 502/504s from hosted API when sending large streaming requests (~1.1-1.4MB payloads). Happens in eu1 and us-east. gave sample req-id acme-req-8732
jamal: can you paste the exact curl + headers and the trace id? any error ids from their client?
emma: here is the minimal repro they used:
```bash
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXX' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'X-Request-ID: acme-req-8732' --data @big_payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
emma: client says it starts streaming and then gets a 502 from endpoint after ~8-12s. trace id from our logs: trace=acme-trace-20260315-01
jamal: pulled ingress logs for trace acme-trace-20260315-01 — saw multiple upstream resets + envoy drain events. snippet:
```
[ingress] 1784512410 trace=acme-trace-20260315-01 upstream_reset host=md-backend-12 reason=STREAM_RESET code=RST_STREAM
[ingress] 1784512411 trace=acme-trace-20260315-01 conn_pool: drain initiated for host md-backend-12, active_streams=42
[ingress] 1784512412 trace=acme-trace-20260315-01 upstream_resp_code=502 cluster=frontdoor
```
sofia: runtime note — we rolled a frontdoor autoscaler change last night that shortens graceful drain to 30s to speed scaling. long-lived streaming connections (large payloads) can be ejected mid-stream during scale events and produce 502/504.
jamal: that matches. client long stream + drain = connection reset from upstream. we're seeing an aerosol of ejections in eu1 around 02:00 UTC.
kai: customer asked if it's related to auth rotation — they saw token rotate around same time. we correlate: token rotation triggered background scaleups for tenant.
sofia: action: pinning note — we'll extend drain back to 90s for frontdoor hosts handling streaming traffic, and add a drain-stall metric. creating infra ticket.
sofia: temp mitigation for customers: 1) chunk payloads into smaller streaming messages (<=256KB) 2) add simple client retry on 502 with jittered backoff for streaming restart 3) optionally route to dedicated capacity if they need uninterrupted long streams.
emma: posted mitigation steps to customer and suggested chunking sample: 
```json
{ "chunks": ["<first 256k>", "<next 256k>", "..."], "stream": true }
```
jamal: I've escalated to eng-runtime and created INC-20260315-004 (pinned host drain-timeout tweak + monitor). ticket-bot: INC-20260315-004 created by jamal.
ticket-bot: https://rwd.internal/incidents/INC-20260315-004 (ops only)
deploy-bot: rolling config change to frontdoor drain timeout scheduled to canary at 2026-03-15T04:30Z
sofia: i'll follow up with PR to increase graceful_drain to 90s and add a flag to exempt known streaming routes from rapid scale-down.
jamal: short-term: we turned off the aggressive autoscaler policy for eu1 at 2026-03-15T03:58Z. watching for replays.
emma: customer accepted chunking workaround and asked for ETA. i told them we expect mitigation to be canaried within 3h and full rollout in 24h, and that we can route them to dedicated capacity if they want immediate SLA.
kai: customer will try chunking and report back. assigned follow-up to emma.
sofia: post-mortem items: (1) drain-time config should be workload-aware, (2) surface long-stream percentage in console per-tenant, (3) add automatic routing fallback to dedicated pool for sustained long streams.
emma: closing loop with customer now. will update thread with their verification result.
